logline: In a hamlet where everyone gives a giant stone statue one year on their birthday so nobody gets old, the statue loses a wrinkle every morning; the kid follows Mom before sunrise and sees a wrinkle slide off the stone onto her face: she is taking her years back to grow old with Dad.
question: why is the statue getting younger?
premise: Stonefold, a hamlet on the High Meadow: everyone gives the giant stone face one year on their birthday, and nobody gets old. Only Dad has grey hair: he never gave a year. Now the statue loses one wrinkle every morning (seven this week), Mom slips out before sunrise every day, and today Mom has a grey hair she hides under her hat.
twist: Mom is taking her years back from the statue, one every morning, so she can grow old next to Dad. The kid says what she sees: 'a wrinkle slid off the stone, onto HER face'; then Dad is already waiting on the statue's bench, and the sting: 'Nobody gets old in my village. Except Mom. And Dad.'
mood_note: a light mystery (the kid's bright puzzle), warm and a little tearful on the reveal; never scary
payoff_note: `wrinkle`: the stunt mark in S10 when Mom's skin takes the brow line and second streak, on L10's FACE (the hit and the picture change; L10 is the reveal SAID: what the kid sees). L11 (the one beat, echoing L01) plays over S11; the Short ends 1.0 s after L11.
punch_note: hook L01, the climax L09, the reveal L10

lines.text: In my village, / NOBODY gets old, / except the STATUE. / And it's getting YOUNGER.
lines.say: In my village, nobody gets old, except the statue. And it's getting younger.
lines.direction: flat and matter-of-fact, like any kid's normal; puzzled lift on YOUNGER
lines.note: hook (STANDARDS 0u/0v/0w): the genre opener, the impossible fact, and a short clause that makes it stranger; no stock why tag. On YOUNGER the push reaches the brow: 12 dark wrinkle rows and 7 pale clean stripes where rows were.

lines.text: Every BIRTHDAY, / you give it / a YEAR. / One more WRINKLE.
lines.say: Every birthday, you give it a year. One more wrinkle.
lines.direction: quick, explaining the obvious to a friend
lines.note: the rule in action, shown once: the neighbour's sparkle trail goes FROM her TO the stone and a wrinkle row appears (the reveal runs the same trail the other way)

lines.text: But every MORNING, / a wrinkle's GONE. / SEVEN this week.
lines.say: But every morning, a wrinkle's gone. Seven this week.

lines.text: Just RAIN. / Wears the stone SMOOTH.
lines.say: Just RAIN. Wears the stone SMOOTH.
lines.direction: easy and teasing, not looking up from his bread
lines.note: Dad's one line (critic r1 should-fix: his own voice, and it answers 'why would rain do that?'), on screen. Two-way clue 1: the S03 lapse has seven clear mornings, no rain.

lines.text: Only DAD / has grey hair. / He's NEVER given / a year. / He FORGETS, / I think.
lines.say: Only Dad has grey hair. He's never given a year. He forgets, I think.
lines.direction: fond eye-roll at a silly dad; the misreading said like it's obvious
lines.note: clue 2 (he chose to get old) with its innocent misreading

lines.text: And Mom goes on a WALK. / Every DAY.
lines.say: And Mom goes on a walk. Every day.
lines.note: clue 3 (critic r1: no longer echoes L03's 'every MORNING'; S06 still shows her leaving at pre-dawn, unsaid)

lines.direction: breezy and quick, a wink in it
lines.note: Mom's one line, on screen at the door at sunrise (critic r1: her own voice, not 'sweetie'). Two-way: she says the opposite of what she's doing.

lines.text: Today / Mom had / a GREY hair. / She hid it / under her HAT. / I think / she's EMBARRASSED.
lines.say: Today Mom had a grey hair. She hid it under her hat. I think she's embarrassed.
lines.direction: bright and sympathetic, a giggle on EMBARRASSED, never worried
lines.note: clue 4 (the critic's fix: bright, not scared). Decoy read: she is sick, or paying Dad's share.

lines.text: So before SUNRISE, / I followed her. / Where does she even WALK?
lines.say: So before sunrise, I followed her. Where does she even walk?
lines.direction: sneaky-proud, bright, full voice; the question up and curious
lines.note: the climax: the narrator says she wants to know (critic r1 blocker) and goes to look

lines.text: She touched the STATUE, / and a wrinkle slid / off the STONE, / onto HER face.
lines.say: She touched the statue, and a wrinkle slid off the stone, onto her face.
lines.direction: slower, wide-eyed, saying exactly what she sees; FACE lands with the close-up
lines.note: the reveal SAID (story_format 6, critic r1): the trail runs stone -> Mom (S02 reversed); she turns east on STONE; push to her face on FACE: a new dark brow line and a second grey streak (statue_mom_2); payoff mark `wrinkle`. The kid says what she sees; the viewer makes the jump to Dad in S11.

lines.text: NOBODY gets old / in my village. / Except MOM. / And DAD.
lines.say: Nobody gets old in my village. Except Mom. And Dad.
lines.direction: the sting, quiet and proud, a tiny smile; cut 1 s after DAD
lines.note: the one beat: echoes L01 ('nobody gets old, except the statue') and loops into it; said over Dad on the bench turning to Mom
